title: MLB Plaintext Play-by-Play Viewer
description: Searchable web viewer and reproducible archive pipeline for MLB regular-season and postseason games from 2014 forward, using exactly one source: HTTPS responses from MLB's own statsapi.mlb.com domain. It does not invent, estimate, silently repair or manually enter a score, name, play or measurement — the raw download is the exact official response body and the human-readable files are deterministic projections of fields in that response. It browses the official schedule by date and includes MLB sportId=1 game types R, F, D, L and W (regular season and postseason) while excluding Spring Training, exhibitions and the All-Star Game, renders line scores, decisions, every play, pitch and action details, runner movements and batting and pitching box scores, searches a game's official descriptions and player names in the browser, and downloads a readable .txt report, the complete raw .json or an event-oriented .ndjson without a server or account. A bulk archive runs from January 1, 2014 through any requested end date with retries, rate limiting, resume support, provenance checks and checksums, live games refresh automatically using the wait interval returned in MLB's feed, and while a game is Live the pipeline logs transient official events — score changes, official-scorer ruling changes, scoring-pending rulings and boundary calls — into a per-game Event log tab stored locally in the browser so it can be reopened after the event or the game is over. A response is accepted only if the URL is HTTPS on the exact statsapi.mlb.com host, the response is successful JSON, it contains MLB Advanced Media's provenance notice, and a game feed's returned gamePk matches the requested gamePk. The site has no sample scores and no fallback dataset: if the official endpoint cannot be reached or does not return a value, the interface says so. The repository does not relicense MLB data — every saved record keeps MLB Advanced Media's returned notice, the exact source URL, the UTC retrieval time and a SHA-256 digest, and users remain responsible for complying with MLB's terms. The site is dependency-free static HTML, CSS and JavaScript in docs/ that requests data directly from MLB in the visitor's browser, with no third-party analytics, proxy, database, generated game content, logo or team artwork. Both test suites were executed here: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` reports Ran 6 tests, OK, and `node --test tests/test_eventlog.mjs` reports 15 tests, 15 pass, 0 fail.
